recognize_zh: 一群異常細胞，核凹折或分葉，部分細胞質可見細小粉紅至紅紫色顆粒，但沒有典型 APL 那種密集粗大顆粒，符合微顆粒型 APL（M3v）。
features: Cluster of about six medium to large abnormal cells
Irregular, indented to bilobed nuclei with fine chromatin
Moderate pale blue cytoplasm; several cells show fine, dust-like pink azurophilic granules
Granules sparse and fine rather than coarse and nucleus-obscuring
No definite Auer rod bundles identified
Background red cells without notable schistocytes; platelets scant
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a cluster of abnormal medium to large cells with moderate pale blue cytoplasm. Nuclei are irregular with folded or bilobed contours and finely dispersed chromatin. A subset of cells contains fine, dust-like azurophilic granules, while others appear nearly agranular; coarse granules and faggot cells are not seen. Findings are consistent with acute promyelocytic leukemia, hypogranular (microgranular) variant, which requires emergent confirmation of PML::RARA and assessment for coagulopathy.

ddx.vs: Monocytic blasts can have folded nuclei and fine granules, but they are nonspecific esterase positive with CD14/CD64 and HLA-DR expression, whereas APL-v is strongly MPO positive, HLA-DR negative, and PML::RARA positive.
Normal promyelocytes have round eccentric nuclei with a paranuclear hof and nucleoli, not the bilobed butterfly-shaped nuclei of APL-v cells.
Reactive left shift shows a spectrum of maturation with myelocytes and band forms rather than a monomorphous population of immature cells with bilobed nuclei.
